candidates.workflow_title: End-to-End E-Discovery Lifecycle (Legal Hold to Production)
candidates.occupation_scope: E-discovery specialist or litigation support analyst managing the EDRM lifecycle for a matter.
candidates.workflow_summary: Execute the EDRM stages (identification, legal-hold preservation, forensic collection, processing, review, analysis, production) to deliver a defensible Bates-numbered production set with load files and metadata.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Custodian list and data map; legal-hold scope from counsel; native documents (email, chat, files) from client systems; discovery requests, court order, and ESI protocol.
candidates.usage_permissions: Client-authorized data export and processing rights; chain-of-custody documentation; production strictly per court order and agreed ESI protocol.
candidates.task_input: A corpus of potentially relevant ESI plus custodians, date ranges, and the discovery requests or preservation order defining scope.
candidates.professional_operations: Identify custodians and data sources; issue and track legal holds; collect with chain of custody; process and normalize into a review platform; cull via search and deduplication; review for responsiveness; produce with Bates numbering and load files.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A defensible production set (images or natives, metadata load file, privilege log) plus preservation and collection logs.
candidates.success_criteria: All responsive, non-privileged ESI produced within deadlines with intact chain of custody and metadata, defensible against spoliation challenges.
candidates.verification_approach: A scripted pipeline reproduces hold notices, deduplication, search culling, and load-file generation from a seeded corpus and is diffed against a reference production set.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Proprietary review platforms (Relativity, Everlaw) are typical but the core pipeline is reproducible on Linux with Python; GPU optional for AI ranking; Windows rarely required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary platform licenses and privileged/confidential data access are the main blockers; native file-type parsing (PST, chat) can be brittle.
candidates.expert_capability: E-discovery specialist or litigation support analyst who knows FRCP discovery rules, ESI protocols, and review-platform administration.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Touches business_finance/compliance when the matter is a regulatory investigation rather than civil litigation.
candidates.granularity_check: The whole EDRM lifecycle is appropriately end-to-end; single sub-stages such as legal hold alone would be too granular.
candidates.pending_confirmation: EDRM stage list should be confirmed against the full EDRM page (fetched but truncated this round).

candidates.workflow_title: Privilege Review and Privilege Log Generation
candidates.occupation_scope: Privilege review attorney or document review attorney producing a defensible privilege log.
candidates.workflow_summary: Screen a review population for attorney-client privilege and work product, apply privilege codes, withhold privileged documents from production, and generate a privilege log describing withheld items.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Privilege criteria and custodians (attorneys, clients); list of in-house and outside counsel email domains; a review platform with coded documents; negotiated privilege-log fields.
candidates.usage_permissions: Attorney-supervised review; privilege-log fields negotiated with opposing counsel; withheld content must remain inaccessible to the receiving party.
candidates.task_input: A review population of documents plus defined privilege types (attorney-client, work product) and the negotiated privilege-log field list.
candidates.professional_operations: Define privilege codes and criteria; search for attorney-involved communications; apply privilege and type codes across attachment families and email threads; configure withholding rules; emit the privilege log with descriptions.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A privilege log spreadsheet listing withheld documents with Bates numbers and privilege descriptions, plus production placeholders for withheld items.
candidates.success_criteria: No privileged content is produced, every withheld document appears in the log with a valid description, and all coding is auditable.
candidates.verification_approach: Seeded privilege codes propagate to attachment families and email threads, and the generated log output matches expected withheld-item entries and descriptions.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux with Python is sufficient for log generation from coding metadata; proprietary platforms (Everlaw, Relativity) provide native tooling; GPU optional for predictive privilege ranking.
candidates.blocking_risks: Access to real privileged documents is highly restricted; platform licensing; QC for false-positive privilege calls.
candidates.expert_capability: Privilege review attorney or senior review manager who knows attorney-client and work-product doctrine plus log conventions.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps business_finance/compliance when privilege applies to regulatory production; the privilege-doctrine basis overlaps legal_research.
candidates.granularity_check: Privilege review plus log generation is a complete sub-workflow distinct from general responsiveness review.
candidates.pending_confirmation: None; source read in full this round.

candidates.workflow_title: Technology-Assisted Review (TAR) Responsiveness and Issue Coding
candidates.occupation_scope: Document review manager or e-discovery consultant running a predictive-coding validation workflow.
candidates.workflow_summary: Train a predictive-coding model on seed reviewer decisions to rank documents by responsiveness, apply issue codes, and validate via statistical sampling and QC instead of full linear review.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Responsiveness and issue code definitions; a representative seed set of coded documents; production protocol; sampling and validation statistics thresholds.
candidates.usage_permissions: Attorney oversight of the model; defensibility requires documented methodology, seed coding, and a validation sample.
candidates.task_input: A large uncoded document population, issue and responsiveness code definitions, and an initial seed of reviewer-coded examples.
candidates.professional_operations: Build a training seed; train the predictive model; rank and prioritize documents; apply suggested codes; sample and validate low-confidence bins; escalate to human QC; produce the validated responsive set.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A validated responsive document set with issue codes and a defensibility memo documenting methodology and measured recall and precision.
candidates.success_criteria: Recall meets agreed thresholds with documented validation, and the review is defensible under judicial or regulatory scrutiny.
candidates.verification_approach: Ranking and sampling are reproduced from a labeled benchmark and recall, precision, and elusion are measured against a known ground-truth set.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux with Python ML is feasible; proprietary TAR tools (Relativity, Everlaw, Lighthouse IQ) are common; GPU useful for large models.
candidates.blocking_risks: Ground-truth labels are confidential and hard to obtain; defensibility documentation burden; proprietary tool access.
candidates.expert_capability: Review manager or e-discovery consultant fluent in TAR methodology, sampling statistics, and defensibility standards.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Shares the document-review population with privilege review (wf02) and with business_finance/compliance investigation review.
candidates.granularity_check: TAR is a distinct complete workflow, not a parameter variant of linear review.
candidates.pending_confirmation: Confirm specific recall and precision thresholds with an expert.

candidates.occupation_scope: Litigation paralegal or associate attorney preparing a witness for deposition.
candidates.workflow_summary: Assemble case documents and exhibits, draft a witness examination outline anchored to key documents and a timeline, and prepare exhibit binders for a deposition.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Deposition notice and topics; witness documents and prior statements; case timeline and key exhibits; privilege and confidentiality constraints.
candidates.usage_permissions: Counsel-prepared work product; exhibits cleared for use under protective order; witness access to authorized materials only.
candidates.task_input: A deposition notice listing topics, the witness's relevant documents, and the case timeline and issues.
candidates.professional_operations: Identify key documents and anchor points; build a chronology; draft the examination outline with exhibit cross-references; assemble exhibit binders; flag impeachment and privilege-sensitive material.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A deposition outline with exhibit list, a prepared exhibit binder, and a witness-preparation summary.
candidates.success_criteria: Every notice topic is covered, each outline point is anchored to a specific document, and exhibits are correctly ordered and cleared.
candidates.verification_approach: A generated outline maps each question area to a cited exhibit and the exhibit list reconciles with the source document set.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Office-document tooling (docx and pdf) suffices; Linux with Python fine; no GPU or proprietary software strictly required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Low technical blockers; accuracy depends on authentic case documents and attorney framing that a synthetic task must supply.
candidates.expert_capability: Litigation paralegal or associate with deposition practice and document-management skills.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Uses documents drawn from the e-discovery and document-review population (wf01 through wf03).
candidates.granularity_check: Deposition support is a complete pre-trial work product, not a single operation.

candidates.occupation_scope: Research attorney or law clerk drafting an objective legal memorandum.
candidates.workflow_summary: Research governing authorities and draft an objective memo using the IRAC structure (question presented, brief answer, facts, issue-by-issue rule, application, analysis, and conclusion).
candidates.expert_raw_materials: The client fact pattern; governing jurisdiction; identified statutes, regulations, and cases; the legal question to be answered.
candidates.usage_permissions: Firm-internal work product; authorities from licensed legal databases or public sources; citation to primary law only.
candidates.task_input: A concrete fact pattern and a well-defined legal question within a named jurisdiction.
candidates.professional_operations: Spot issues and identify governing law; research primary authorities; synthesize rules; apply law to facts issue by issue; draft and bluebook-cite the memo.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A structured legal memorandum with question presented, brief answer, facts, analysis, and conclusion, fully cited.
candidates.success_criteria: Every issue is addressed, rules are correctly stated and applied to the facts, and all propositions are supported by primary authority.
candidates.verification_approach: Structural checks confirm memo parts, citation presence, and that each analysis section cites a rule source; legal-reasoning correctness requires expert grading.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux with Python fine for text and structure checks; research typically needs Westlaw or LexisNexis subscriptions (proprietary).
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary legal-database access for authoritative case and statute text; grading legal correctness needs a qualified attorney.
candidates.expert_capability: Research attorney, associate, or law clerk skilled in doctrinal analysis and legal citation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps business_finance/compliance when the memo analyzes a regulatory rule, and litigation when it supports a motion.
candidates.granularity_check: Full memo drafting is end-to-end; isolated IRAC paragraphs would be too granular.
candidates.pending_confirmation: Source URLs located via search and partially fetched; confirm the memo-part list against the live legalwriting.net page.

candidates.occupation_scope: Law librarian or research attorney compiling a legislative history report for a statute.
candidates.workflow_summary: Trace a statutory section to its public law and bill, then gather committee reports, hearings, floor debates, and signing statements into a documented legislative history.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: The statute or U.S. Code citation; access to Congress.gov, committee reports, the Congressional Record, and presidential signing statements.
candidates.usage_permissions: Public government documents; the compiled history is attorney work product for the requesting matter.
candidates.task_input: A specific statutory section or public-law citation whose legislative history must be reconstructed.
candidates.professional_operations: Identify public-law and bill numbers; locate committee reports, hearings, debates, and signing statements; assemble them in chronological order; annotate each source's relevance.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A legislative history report listing and excerpting the key documents in order with citations.
candidates.success_criteria: All material legislative-history documents for the provision are located and correctly cited, with no fabricated sources.
candidates.verification_approach: Each cited document resolves to a real Congress.gov or GPO record, and the trace steps (statute to public law to bill) are reproducible.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux with Python and public web (Congress.gov, GPO, LOC) suffice; no GPU or proprietary software required.
candidates.blocking_risks: Low blockers; accuracy hinges on distinguishing authoritative documents from summaries and commentary.
candidates.expert_capability: Law librarian or research attorney who knows the legislative process and document hierarchy.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Feeds statutory-interpretation analysis (wf03) and litigation when legislative intent is argued.
candidates.granularity_check: Compiling a full history is end-to-end; citing a single committee report would be too narrow.
candidates.pending_confirmation: None; LOC guide read in full this round.

candidates.occupation_scope: Doctrinal legal researcher or associate analyzing how a statute applies to a fact pattern.
candidates.workflow_summary: Apply statutory-interpretation methods (plain meaning and, where ambiguous, legislative history and canons) to determine how a statute governs a specific fact pattern.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Statute text and structure; the specific fact pattern; prior interpretations (case law, agency guidance); relevant legislative history if the text is ambiguous.
candidates.usage_permissions: Primary statute and case law from licensed databases; the interpretation memo is attorney work product.
candidates.task_input: A statutory provision and a fact pattern raising an interpretive question.
candidates.professional_operations: Parse statutory text and definitions; assess ambiguity; apply plain-meaning and canons; consult legislative history and precedents; state the controlling interpretation and its consequences.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A written interpretation memo stating the operative construction, reasoning, and authority for each step.
candidates.success_criteria: The interpretation is textually grounded, consistent with controlling precedent, and each interpretive step is supported by authority.
candidates.verification_approach: The memo cites the statute and any controlling case, and structure checks confirm the reasoning chain; substantive correctness requires expert review.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Linux with Python for structure checks; Westlaw or LexisNexis subscriptions for authoritative precedents are a practical dependency.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary database access; interpretive correctness cannot be mechanically verified and needs expert grading.
candidates.expert_capability: Doctrinal researcher or associate fluent in canons of construction and controlling-precedent analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Directly overlaps business_finance/compliance (regulatory interpretation) and litigation (statutory arguments).
candidates.granularity_check: A full interpretation memo is end-to-end; a single canon applied in isolation would be too narrow.
candidates.pending_confirmation: The canons-of-construction framework is partly E4 (no direct fetched source this round); confirm the canon list with an expert.

candidates.occupation_scope: Research attorney or law clerk verifying whether a case remains good law.
candidates.workflow_summary: Run a citator on a case, interpret positive and negative treatment symbols, and produce a precedential-validity assessment for the specific proposition being relied upon.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: The case citation; the specific proposition or headnote being relied on; access to a citator (Shepard's or KeyCite).
candidates.usage_permissions: Citator is a proprietary subscription service; the resulting validity memo is attorney work product.
candidates.task_input: A case citation and the narrow proposition for which it is being cited.
candidates.professional_operations: Run the citator; review subsequent history and citing decisions; distinguish negative treatment of the case from negative treatment of the specific proposition; note pending cases and jurisdiction.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A validity memo stating whether the case and proposition are still good law, with the treatment history summarized and cited.
candidates.success_criteria: The good-law determination is correct for the cited proposition and every treatment claim traces to a real subsequent case.
candidates.verification_approach: Each cited subsequent case is cross-checked against a public citation graph (for example CourtListener) to confirm it exists and cites the target.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Proprietary citator (Westlaw KeyCite or Lexis Shepard's) is the standard; a Linux with Python pipeline over a public citation graph is a feasible proxy.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary citator access; distinguishing proposition-level from case-level treatment is error-prone.
candidates.expert_capability: Research attorney or law clerk who can read citator symbols and apply proposition-level analysis.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps litigation (case law research for motions) and doctrinal research generally.
candidates.granularity_check: A citator validity memo is a complete research deliverable, not a single lookup.
candidates.pending_confirmation: Source URLs consulted via search; confirm symbol meanings against the live UC Law article.
